<action type="say">
When I query a *status* feed with a flight number + date and get nothing back, it usually means one of these:

1) The flight isn’t in the live-status data yet  
   - Often true for flights far in the future or for flights whose schedule hasn’t been fully loaded or finalized in the status system.

2) It exists but under a different “operating” number  
   - Typical for codeshares: your email shows QF7712, but operationally it might be, say, AA1234 or CX567 that will show up in status tools.

3) It’s a non‑standard/charter/special service  
   - Those can show in bookings but not always in public status feeds.

So yes: with only `QF7712 + 2026-09-14`, the “no result” most commonly points to “not loaded yet here” or “codeshare/operating under another number,” not “fake flight.”

On the two things you care about:
- **Rough time of day:** I can’t reliably infer that from the number alone; airlines don’t encode departure time in the numeric part of the flight number in any consistent way.
- **On‑time vs delayed:** That’s only knowable close to departure; far ahead, no system (including this one) can give a meaningful on‑time prediction.

Once you’re at a computer (or later on your phone) you can quickly sanity‑check it by:
- Searching the airline’s site or Google for `QF7712 14 September 2026` (or your departure/arrival cities + date), or  
- Using “Manage booking” with your confirmation code and last name to see the exact route and scheduled times.

If you remember even roughly what cities it’s between (e.g., “Sydney to Melbourne domestic” or “US to Australia”), tell me and I can at least outline how that kind of flight typically looks (duration, usual time bands, etc.), but I still won’t be able to say anything real about delays yet.</action>
